newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Witness tackles lawyer in S.Africa hit-squad probe.
newsitem.headline: Witness tackles lawyer in S.Africa hit-squad probe.

text.p: A lawyer acting for South Africa's former police minister Adriaan Vlok was accused by a self-confessed Zulu hit-squad leader on Thursday of withholding the truth about hit-squad operations.

The accusation was made by Gcina Mkhize, an Inkatha Freedom Party hit-squad leader trained by the apartheid-era army in the mid-1980s, during a Truth and Reconciliation Commission hearing into the party's death squads in KwaZulu-Natal province.

Mkhize, who was giving testimony on the alleged systematic murder of Inkatha's political opponents, said lawyer Louis Visser supplied false information to the Goldstone Commission judicial probe which ran from 1991 to 1994.
"You are still on a mission of hiding the truth away from the public... If there is to be reconciliation you should start talking the truth," Mkhize said to applause from the audience.

The Goldstone Commission, headed by Judge Richard Goldstone who later worked as a senior prosecutor for the Bosnian war crimes tribunal, investigated allegations of state-sanctioned hit-squads operating against the African National Congress.

"I would like to remind you that you yourself were involved in trying to give false information to the Goldstone Commission," Mkhize said in reply to Visser's statement that Mkhize was giving different information to the truth body than that he gave to Goldstone.

Visser denied Mkhize's allegations, saying he had merely taken and prepared statements on behalf of KwaZulu government and Inkatha members implicated in the covert training by the military in Namibia's Caprivi Strip in 1986.
Mkhize testified he had taken orders for political killings from Inkatha leaders in the once semi-autonomous KwaZulu region.
"They (the leaders) said the ANC had very influential people and we had to start to eliminate them. They made that very clear to me," Mkhize said in his testimony.

Inkatha, led by Chief Mangosuthu Buthelezi, is a minority partner in the coalition government under President Nelson Mandela's ANC. The two parties' supporters are still fighting a low-level turf war in KwaZulu-Natal province.
